findings.finding: F2's fix assumes Mattermost's GET /channels/:id/posts?since= endpoint is inclusive of the boundary (fetches posts at exactly `lastSeen.ms`, then dedupes the already-processed post by id: `getPostsSince(dmChannelId, lastSeen.ms)` followed by `fetched.filter(p => p.id !== lastSeen.id)`). Mattermost's own API reference and server source say otherwise: the `since` query param is documented as selecting 'posts modified after that time' (exclusive), and the actual server-side filter is `WHERE UpdateAt > ? AND ChannelId = ?` (strict greater-than, and on UpdateAt rather than createAt). Under that semantics, calling with `since = lastSeen.ms` returns only posts with update_at > lastSeen.ms -- it will never include the previously-processed post itself, and, critically, it will also never include a sibling post whose create_at (and unedited update_at) equals lastSeen.ms exactly. That sibling is excluded by the server before the client's dedupe-by-id filter ever runs, so the client-side dedupe never has anything to do in the common case. The literal scenario F2 was filed for -- two posts sharing the same create_at millisecond as the persisted watermark -- is therefore still silently dropped; the fix changed the request's boundary math (`ms` instead of `ms + 1`) without changing the outcome for that scenario, because the server's own boundary is already exclusive.
findings.evidence: Mattermost API reference (mattermost-api-reference/v4/source/posts.yaml, `since` param): 'Provide a non-zero value in Unix time milliseconds to select posts modified after that time' -- 'after', not 'at or after'. Mattermost server source (server/channels/store/sqlstore/post_store.go, GetPostsSince): the CTE's WHERE clause is `UpdateAt > ? AND ChannelId = ?` (strict `>`, filtered on UpdateAt not CreateAt). No test in this repo exercises the real HTTP filtering semantics for this boundary -- daemon.test.ts's dedupe test (src/daemon.test.ts, 'catches up ... deduping the already-processed post by id') mocks restClient.getPostsSince to unconditionally return the same-ms sibling regardless of the `since` value passed, so it cannot catch a mismatch between the assumed and actual API semantics; mattermostRestClient.test.ts's msw handlers likewise return whatever the test tells them to, not a filtered response, so neither test layer would fail even though the real Mattermost server would still drop the sibling post.
findings.expected: Track completeness some way that doesn't depend on the server including the watermark post itself in the response -- e.g. persist the last-seen id and, on catch-up, treat any returned post with `createAt <= lastSeen.ms` and `id !== lastSeen.id` as still-missed (rather than relying on inclusive refetch-and-dedupe), or query with `since = lastSeen.ms - 1` and dedupe everything at or before `lastSeen.ms` whose id isn't `lastSeen.id`, so a same-millisecond sibling is fetched rather than filtered out server-side before the client ever sees it.
findings.note: daemon.ts catchUp() now queries getPostsSince(dmChannelId, lastSeen.ms - 1) when lastSeen.id is present (was lastSeen.ms), accounting for Mattermost's server-side exclusive `since` boundary (WHERE UpdateAt > ?) so a post sharing the watermark's exact millisecond is actually returned by the server. Dedupe is unchanged (fetched.filter(p => p.id !== lastSeen.id)) -- with the corrected since value it now has a same-ms sibling to actually act on. Legacy id===null path (ms + 1) is untouched, as that boundary was never the issue. Added a daemon.test.ts case whose getPostsSince mock filters by the actual `since` argument passed (post.createAt > since), reproducing the real server's strict-exclusive filtering instead of unconditionally returning the sibling; verified by temporarily reverting daemon.ts and confirming the new test fails (asserts since=4999, old code passes 5000) before re-applying the fix, at which point the full suite (56 tests) and tsc --noEmit both pass clean.
